propertyTax.text: The Homestead Market Value Exclusion reduces the taxable market value of qualifying homesteads. The full 40% exclusion (maximum $38,000) applies to homesteads valued at $95,000 or less, and it phases out for homesteads valued at $517,200 or more.
propertyTax.source: Minnesota Department of Revenue: homestead market value exclusion
propertyTax.quote: For homesteads valued at $95,000 or less, the exclusion is 40% of the market value, creating a maximum exclusion of $38,000. | The exclusion is reduced as property values increase and phases out for homesteads valued at $517,200 or more.

closing.text: Minnesota's state deed tax rate is 0.0033 (0.33%) of the net consideration, and the state mortgage registry tax rate is 0.0023 (0.23%) of the debt secured by the mortgage. Both are paid to the county where the document is recorded.
closing.source: Minnesota Department of Revenue: mortgage registry and deed tax
closing.quote: The Deed Tax rate is 0.0033 of the net consideration. | The state Mortgage Tax rate is 0.0023 of the debt that is being secured by a mortgage on Minnesota real property. | It is collected and paid to the Minnesota county where the conveyance document is being recorded.

programs.text: Mississippi Home Corporation has programs that offer cash assistance at closing. All MHC products require pre-purchase homebuyer education, and some require first-time buyer status in certain counties.
programs.quote: We have programs that will offer you cash assistance at closing | All MHC products require that you complete pre-purchase homebuyer education.

programs.text: The Home4All program provides up to $25,000 in homebuyer assistance. Down payment assistance cannot exceed 50% of the purchase price, and the amount is based on the homebuyer's need.
programs.quote: The Home4All program is designed to assist people to become homeowners by providing up to $25,000 in homebuyer assistance. | Downpayment assistance cannot exceed 50% of the purchase price.

programs.text: Home4All requires household income below 80% of median income, adjusted for family size, and that the buyer has not owned or had an interest in a principal residence within the past three years.
programs.quote: Household income must be below 80% of median income, adjusted for family size. | Cannot have owned or had an interest in a principal residence within the past three years.

propertyTax.text: Mississippi's homestead exemption gives eligible applicants a tax credit of up to $300 (based on property value) against taxes due on the property.
propertyTax.source: Mississippi Department of Revenue: homestead exemption
propertyTax.quote: Eligible applicants can receive a tax credit of up to $300 (based on property value) against taxes due on the property.

propertyTax.text: Applicants must own and occupy the home as their primary residence on January 1. Applications are accepted during the filing period of January 1 to April 1.
propertyTax.source: Mississippi Department of Revenue: homestead exemption
propertyTax.quote: Applicants must own and occupy their home as their primary residence on January 1 | during the designated filing period (January 1 – April 1).

propertyTax.text: Applicants who are at least 65, or totally disabled, by January 1 are exempt from taxes on the first $7,500 of assessed value of their homestead.
propertyTax.source: Mississippi Department of Revenue: homestead exemption
propertyTax.quote: exempt from taxes on the first $7,500 of assessed value of their homestead.

programs.text: MHDC's First Place program serves potential first-time homebuyers and qualified veterans. It offers the option of cash assistance for down payment and closing costs, with no minimum down payment or minimum loan amount.
programs.quote: potential first-time homebuyers and qualified Veterans | the option for cash assistance to be used for down payment and closing costs | with no minimum down payment or minimum loan amounts

propertyTax.text: The Missouri Property Tax Credit is for certain senior citizens and 100 percent disabled individuals. It is a maximum of $1,100 for owners who owned and occupied their home, and it is based on the real estate taxes paid and total household income.
propertyTax.source: Missouri Department of Revenue: property tax credit
propertyTax.quote: certain senior citizens and 100 percent disabled individuals | The credit is for a maximum of $750 for renters and $1,100 for owners who owned and occupied their home. | is based on the amount of real estate taxes or rent paid and total household income

closing.text: Nevada's real property transfer tax rate is $1.95 for every $500 of the property's value, or any fraction of $500. The county recorder collects it when the transfer documents are recorded.
closing.source: Nevada Department of Taxation: real property transfer tax
closing.quote: the rate is $1.95 for every $500 of the property's value or any fraction thereof

closing.text: Washoe and Churchill counties add $0.10 to the base rate, and Clark County adds $0.60.
closing.source: Nevada Department of Taxation: real property transfer tax
closing.quote: An additional $0.10 is added to the base rate. | An additional $0.60 is added to the base rate.

agency.name: New Jersey Housing and Mortgage Finance Agency (NJHMFA)

programs.text: NJHMFA's Down Payment Assistance Program provides qualified buyers up to $15,000 based on the county of the property being purchased, as an interest-free, five-year forgivable second loan with no monthly payment.
programs.quote: provides qualified buyers with up to $15,000 based upon the county of the property being purchased. | an interest-free, five-year forgivable second loan with no monthly payment.

programs.text: NJHMFA considers you a first-time homebuyer if you have not owned a home within the previous three years.
programs.quote: You're considered a first-time homebuyer if you have not owned a home within the previous three years.

propertyTax.text: New Jersey's homeowner property tax relief programs include ANCHOR, Stay NJ and the Senior Freeze.
propertyTax.source: NJ Division of Taxation: property tax relief programs
propertyTax.quote: The Fiscal Year 2027 budget provides property tax relief benefits for the Senior Freeze, ANCHOR, and Stay NJ programs.

closing.text: New Jersey charges the seller a Realty Transfer Fee for recording the deed, calculated on the consideration stated in the deed.
closing.source: NJ Division of Taxation: realty transfer fee
closing.quote: The State imposes a Realty Transfer Fee (RTF) on the seller of real property for recording a deed for the sale. | The RTF is calculated based on the amount of consideration recited in the deed

closing.text: A Graduated Percent Fee also applies to sales of Class 2 residential property above $1,000,000. It starts at 1% of total consideration between $1,000,000 and $2,000,000 and rises in higher tiers, to 3.5% above $3.5 million. The seller is statutorily responsible for it.
closing.source: NJ Division of Taxation: realty transfer fee
closing.quote: 1% of total consideration if in excess of $1,000,000 but not in excess of $2,000,000; | The seller is statutorily responsible for the RTF and the Graduated Percent Fee. | 3.5% of total consideration if in excess of $3,500,000.

programs.text: FirstHome is a mortgage loan program for first-time New Mexico homebuyers with low to moderate incomes. FirstDown, a fixed-rate second mortgage, provides down payment and closing cost assistance and must be combined with FirstHome.
programs.quote: FirstHome is a mortgage loan program for first-time New Mexico homebuyers with low to moderate incomes.

programs.text: HomeNow is a down payment and closing cost second mortgage loan for first-time buyers with lower household incomes. The loan has a 0% interest rate and may be forgiven after 10 years if certain conditions are met.
programs.quote: The loan has a 0% interest rate and may be forgiven after 10 years if certain conditions are met.

programs.text: The programs page lists a minimum credit score of 620 and requires all homebuyers to receive pre-purchase homebuyer counseling.
programs.quote: A minimum credit score of 620 is required. | All homebuyers must receive pre-purchase homebuyer counseling.

propertyTax.text: Per the Legislative Finance Committee's May 15, 2024 report, the taxable value of a residential property cannot grow by more than 3 percent each year.
propertyTax.source: New Mexico Legislative Finance Committee: Property Taxes in New Mexico (May 2024)
propertyTax.quote: Simply put, the taxable value of a residential property cannot grow by more than 3 percent each year.

propertyTax.text: Heads of household are allowed a $2,000 exemption on the taxable value of residential property for a primary home (as of the committee's May 2024 report).
propertyTax.source: New Mexico Legislative Finance Committee: Property Taxes in New Mexico (May 2024)
propertyTax.quote: In New Mexico, head of households are allowed a $2,000 exemption on the taxable value of residential property

agency.name: State of New York Mortgage Agency (SONYMA), part of NY Homes and Community Renewal

programs.text: SONYMA's Down Payment Assistance Loan is an enhanced loan of up to $30,000 for low-income first-time home buyers.
programs.source: NY Homes and Community Renewal: SONYMA programs
programs.quote: An enhanced down payment assistance loan of up to $30,000 available to low-income first time home buyers.

programs.text: SONYMA also runs programs for veterans (Homes for Veterans) and for recent college graduates (Graduate to Home Ownership).
programs.source: NY Homes and Community Renewal: SONYMA programs
programs.quote: This program offers low-interest loans for home buying to veterans who have served or currently serving in the armed forces. | This program helps recent college graduates get a home of their own.

propertyTax.text: The School Tax Relief (STAR) program offers property tax relief to eligible New York homeowners. The STAR exemption is no longer available to new homeowners, who can instead register for the STAR credit, which the Tax Department pays by check or direct deposit.
propertyTax.source: NY Department of Taxation and Finance: STAR
propertyTax.quote: The School Tax Relief (STAR) program offers property tax relief to eligible New York State homeowners. | If you are registered for the STAR credit, the Tax Department will issue your STAR benefit via check or direct deposit. | no longer available to new homeowners

propertyTax.text: For the STAR credit, the combined income of the owners and the owners' spouses must be $500,000 or less.
propertyTax.source: NY Department of Taxation and Finance: STAR
propertyTax.quote: the combined income of the owners and the owners' spouses is $500,000 or less

closing.text: New York's mortgage recording tax is made up of a basic tax of 50 cents per $100 of mortgage debt, a special additional tax of 25 cents per $100, and an additional tax of 25 cents per $100 (30 cents per $100 in the Metropolitan Commuter Transportation District). A city or county tax of 25 to 50 cents per $100 applies where it is imposed.
closing.source: NY Department of Taxation and Finance: mortgage recording tax
closing.quote: basic tax of 50 cents per $100 of mortgage debt or obligation secured. | special additional tax of 25 cents per $100 | an additional tax of 25 cents per $100 ... (30 cents per $100 for counties within the Metropolitan Commuter Transportation District). | city or county mortgage tax of 25 to 50 cents per $100 ... where applicable.

closing.text: The state real estate transfer tax is two dollars for each $500 of consideration, or fractional part of it.
closing.source: NY Department of Taxation and Finance: real estate transfer tax
closing.quote: Tax is computed at a rate of two dollars for each $500, or fractional part thereof, of consideration.

closing.text: An additional 1% tax (the "mansion tax") applies to residences sold for $1 million or more.
closing.source: NY Department of Taxation and Finance: real estate transfer tax
closing.quote: An additional tax (mansion tax) of 1% of the sale price applies to residences where consideration is $1 million or more.

programs.text: The NC Home Advantage Mortgage is open to both first-time and move-up buyers and comes with down payment assistance. The assistance is forgiven at 20% per year at the end of years 11 through 15, and repayment is required only if you sell, refinance or transfer the home before year 15.
programs.quote: both first-time and move-up home buyers | forgiven at 20% per year at the end of years 11–15 | Repayment of all of our down payment options is required only if you sell, refinance or transfer your home before year 15.

programs.text: A separate $15,000 down payment option, the NC 1st Home Advantage Down Payment, is limited to first-time buyers and military veterans who meet additional eligibility criteria.
programs.quote: first-time buyers and military veterans who meet additional eligibility criteria | $15,000 option

closing.text: North Carolina charges an excise tax on conveyances of real property of $1.00 on each $500 of consideration or value, paid by the person transferring the property to the register of deeds before the deed is recorded.
closing.source: North Carolina General Statutes § 105-228.30
closing.quote: The tax rate is one dollar ($1.00) on each five hundred dollars ($500.00). | The transferor must pay the tax | The transferor must pay the tax to the register of deeds of the county in which the real estate is located | before recording the instrument of conveyance

programs.text: OHFA's Your Choice! Down Payment Assistance lets buyers choose either 2.5% or 5% of the home's purchase price, and it can go toward the down payment, closing costs or other pre-closing expenses. The assistance is forgiven after seven years. If you sell within seven years, you must repay all of it.
programs.source: OHFA: Your Choice! Down Payment Assistance
programs.quote: allows homebuyers to choose either 2.5% or 5% of the home's purchase price. | Down payment assistance is forgiven after seven years. | If you sell your home within seven years, you must repay all of the assistance provided.

propertyTax.text: Ohio's homestead exemption lets qualifying homeowners exempt some of the market value of their homes from local property taxes. It is for low-income senior citizens, certain permanently and totally disabled Ohioans, and surviving spouses of those individuals.
propertyTax.source: Ohio Department of Taxation: homestead exemption
propertyTax.quote: allows qualifying homeowners to exempt some of the market value of their homes from local property taxes. | low-income senior citizens, certain permanently and totally disabled Ohioans, the surviving spouses of any of those individuals.

propertyTax.text: For tax year 2026 real property, the exemption removes $29,700 of market value for a low-income senior or disabled Ohioan, up from $29,000 for tax year 2025. The income limit for that group is $41,000 for tax year 2026 and $40,000 for tax year 2025.
propertyTax.source: Ohio Department of Taxation: homestead exemption
propertyTax.quote: Low-income senior citizen or disabled Ohioan (excluding a disabled veteran): $29,000 (TY 2025 real property), $29,700 (TY 2026 real property). Income threshold: $40,000 (TY 2025), $41,000 (TY 2026).

propertyTax.text: Applications for real property must be filed on or before December 31 of the year for which the homestead exemption is sought.
propertyTax.source: Ohio Department of Taxation: homestead exemption
propertyTax.quote: Applications for real property must be filed on or before December 31st of the year for which

programs.text: OHFA offers 3.5% down payment assistance toward your total home loan amount at closing, for first-time and repeat buyers, statewide in all 77 counties. Buyers must use an OHFA lending partner.
programs.source: Oklahoma Housing Finance Agency: down payment assistance
programs.quote: 3.5% OHFA down payment assistance toward your total home loan amount at closing. | Available for first-time and repeat buyers. | in all 77 counties

propertyTax.text: The Oklahoma homestead exemption requires that you own and occupy the home as your place of residence on January 1. The application must be filed on or before March 15, or within 30 days of receiving a notice of valuation increase.
propertyTax.source: Oklahoma Tax Commission: homestead exemption application (Form 921)
propertyTax.quote: only if the application is filed on or before March 15 of such year or within thirty (30) days from and after receipt of notice of valuation increase | Homestead exemption cannot be approved if you do not own and occupy the subject property as your place of residence

closing.text: Oklahoma's documentary stamp tax on deeds is 75 cents for each $500 of consideration, or any fractional part of $500.
closing.source: Oklahoma Tax Commission: documentary stamps rules (OAC 710:30)
closing.quote: Stamps worth 75 cents must be affixed for each $500.00 (or any fractional part thereof) of the consideration.

programs.text: Oregon's Down Payment Assistance program provides up to $60,000 or 20% of the purchase price, whichever is less, depending on the program and eligibility requirements.
programs.source: Oregon Housing and Community Services: down payment assistance
programs.quote: up to $60,000 or 20% of the purchase price, whichever is less

programs.text: Buyers must be first-time and/or first-generation homebuyers with income at or below 100% of area median income, complete first-time homebuyer education, and meet with a certified housing counselor.
programs.source: Oregon Housing and Community Services: down payment assistance
programs.quote: first-time and/or first-generation homebuyer | at or below 100% of area median income (AMI) | First-Time Homebuyer Education

programs.text: Flex Lending down payment funds can cover up to 100% of the borrower's cash requirements at closing, as a forgivable second lien with no payments and no interest, or as an amortizing second lien.
programs.source: Oregon Housing and Community Services: down payment assistance
programs.quote: up to 100% of the borrower's cash requirements at closing | a forgivable second lien with no payments and no interest | an amortizing second lien

propertyTax.text: Under Measure 50, growth in a property's maximum assessed value is limited to 3 percent per year. Assessed value, the value used to calculate taxes, can't exceed real market value.
propertyTax.source: Oregon Department of Revenue: maximum assessed value manual
propertyTax.quote: MAV growth is limited to 3 percent per year. | AV is the value used to calculate the taxes assessed on property and can't exceed RMV.

programs.text: The PHFA Grant provides $500 to help with down payment and closing costs.
programs.source: PHFA: assistance loans for home purchase
programs.quote: The PHFA Grant provides grant assistance of $500 to help with downpayment and closing costs

programs.text: The Keystone Forgivable in Ten Years (K-FIT) program provides a second mortgage loan that is forgiven gradually over ten years.
programs.source: PHFA: assistance loans for home purchase
programs.quote: This program provides a second mortgage loan to help buyers supplement the costs of homeownership. (Keystone Forgivable in Ten Years Loan Program (K-FIT))

closing.text: Pennsylvania's realty transfer tax is 1 percent of the value of the real estate.
closing.source: Pennsylvania Department of Revenue: realty transfer tax
closing.quote: Pennsylvania realty transfer tax is imposed at a rate of 1 percent on the value of real estate.

closing.text: County recorders of deeds collect the state tax, often along with an additional local realty transfer tax.
closing.source: Pennsylvania Department of Revenue: realty transfer tax
closing.quote: collected, often along with an additional local realty transfer tax, by county Recorders of Deeds.

agency.name: South Carolina State Housing Finance and Development Authority (SC Housing)

propertyTax.text: South Carolina's homestead exemption, for homeowners over age 65, totally and permanently disabled, or legally blind, completely exempts the first $50,000 of the fair market value of a legal residence from property tax. Contact your county auditor's office to apply.
propertyTax.source: South Carolina Department of Revenue: exempt property
propertyTax.quote: for homeowners over age 65, totally and permanently disabled, or legally blind | The Homestead Exemption is a complete exemption of taxes on the first $50,000 in Fair Market Value of your Legal Residence | Contact your county auditor's office for more information.

closing.text: South Carolina's deed recording fee is $1.85 on realty value of $100 to $500, and $1.85 for each additional $500 increment. The state portion is $1.30 and the county portion is $0.55.
closing.source: South Carolina Department of Revenue: deed recording fee
closing.quote: $1.85 on realty value of $100-$500 | $1.85 for each $500 increments afterwards | The state portion is $1.30 | The county portion is $.55

programs.text: SC Housing's Palmetto Home Advantage offers forgivable down payment assistance of 0%, 3% or 4% of the loan amount with no monthly payment. It is open to first-time, move-up and repeat buyers, with no first-time homebuyer requirement.
programs.quote: forgivable down payment assistance of 0%, 3%, or 4% of the loan amount with no monthly payment. | first-time, move-up and repeat buyers with no first-time home buyer requirements

programs.text: With a THDA Great Choice Home Loan, a deferred down payment option provides up to $6,000 or up to $10,000 as a forgivable second mortgage at 0% interest. It is forgiven after a 10-year term, and the loan is due in full if you sell or refinance before then.
programs.quote: If you qualify for a Great Choice Home Loan | forgivable second mortgage loan | 0% interest | forgiven after a 10-year term | Down Payment Assistance is available up to $6,000 or up to $10,000 in the form of a forgivable second mortgage loan. | Loan is forgiven at the end of 10-year term. | If the home is sold or refinanced prior to 10-year term, the loan is due in full.

programs.text: THDA also offers an amortizing option of up to 5% of the sales price, capped at $15,000, as a 30-year second mortgage loan.
programs.quote: up to 5% of the sales price, capped at $15,000 | second mortgage loan | 30-year amortizing term

propertyTax.text: Tennessee state law provides property tax relief for low-income elderly and disabled homeowners, as well as disabled veteran homeowners or their surviving spouses.
propertyTax.source: Tennessee Comptroller: property tax programs
propertyTax.quote: Tennessee state law provides for property tax relief for low-income elderly and disabled homeowners | as well as disabled veteran homeowners or their surviving spouses.

closing.text: Tennessee's realty transfer tax is $0.37 per $100 of the purchase price.
closing.source: Tennessee Department of Revenue: recordation taxes
closing.quote: $0.37 per $100 of purchase price for the realty transfer

closing.text: The recordation tax on a mortgage or deed of trust is $0.115 per $100 of indebtedness, and the first $2,000 of the debt is exempt.
closing.source: Tennessee Department of Revenue: recordation taxes
closing.quote: $0.115 per $100 of indebtedness. (The first $2,000 of the debt is exempt from taxation.)

programs.text: TSAHC offers homebuyer programs that include down payment assistance and Mortgage Credit Certificates (MCCs).
programs.quote: Down Payment Assistance (DPA) ... Mortgage Credit Certificates (MCCs)

propertyTax.text: School districts must provide a $140,000 exemption on a residence homestead, which is the home you live in as your main residence.
propertyTax.source: Texas Comptroller: property tax exemptions
propertyTax.quote: Tax Code Section 11.13(b) requires school districts to provide a $140,000 exemption on a residence homestead.

propertyTax.text: Homeowners who are 65 or older, or who are disabled, qualify for an additional $60,000 school district exemption.
propertyTax.source: Texas Comptroller: property tax exemptions
propertyTax.quote: Tax Code Section 11.13(c) requires school districts to provide an additional $60,000 residence homestead exemption.

propertyTax.text: The general deadline to file a homestead exemption application is before May 1.
propertyTax.source: Texas Comptroller: property tax exemptions
propertyTax.quote: The general deadline for filing an exemption application is before May 1.

programs.text: Utah Housing Corporation lets eligible buyers borrow their entire minimum required down payment plus all or part of their closing costs on a 30-year fixed-rate second mortgage. You must first qualify for a Utah Housing first mortgage.
programs.source: Utah Housing Corporation: down payment assistance
programs.quote: You may be able to borrow your entire minimum required down payment plus all or a portion of your closing costs | on a Utah Housing Corp 30 year fixed rate second mortgage | you must first qualify for a Utah Housing Corp first mortgage home loan

propertyTax.text: Utah law allows a 45% exemption on the market value of qualifying primary residential property, which reduces taxable value to 55% of fair market value.
propertyTax.source: Utah State Tax Commission: primary residential exemption
propertyTax.quote: 45% exemption on the market value of qualifying primary residential property | This exemption reduces the taxable value of eligible primary residences to 55% of their fair market value.

propertyTax.text: A primary residence is a dwelling occupied as a primary domicile for at least 183 consecutive days in a calendar year. A household can claim only one such exemption in Utah.
propertyTax.source: Utah State Tax Commission: primary residential exemption
propertyTax.quote: occupied as a primary domicile for at least 183 consecutive days in a calendar year | Only one primary residential exemption may be claimed per household within the State of Utah.

programs.text: Virginia Housing's Down Payment Assistance Grant is for qualified first-time homebuyers, or repeat buyers purchasing in Areas of Economic Opportunity, who have a bond FHA or conventional loan from Virginia Housing. It can only be used with eligible Virginia Housing loans, and household income and purchase price must fall within the program's limits.
programs.source: Virginia Housing: Down Payment Assistance Grant
programs.quote: Be a qualified first-time homebuyer or repeat buyer purchasing in Areas of Economic Opportunity | Have a bond FHA/Conventional loan from Virginia Housing | may only be used with eligible Virginia Housing loans

closing.text: Virginia's state recordation tax on a deed is 25 cents on every $100, or fraction of $100, of the deed's consideration or the property's actual value, whichever is greater.
closing.source: Code of Virginia § 58.1-801: Deeds generally; charter amendments
closing.quote: On every deed admitted to record, except a deed exempt from taxation by law, there is hereby levied a state recordation tax. | The rate of the tax shall be 25 cents on every $100 or fraction thereof | of (i) the consideration of the deed or (ii) the actual value of the property conveyed, whichever is greater.

closing.quote: The rate of the tax, when the consideration or value of the interest, whichever is greater, exceeds $100, | shall be 50 cents for each $500 or fraction thereof, | The tax imposed by this section shall be paid by the grantor, or any person who signs on behalf of the grantor,

propertyTax.text: Virginia law lets each locality decide, by ordinance, whether to offer an exemption from, or deferral of, property taxes for people who are at least 65 years of age or who are found to be permanently and totally disabled. propertyTax.source: Code of Virginia § 58.1-3210: Exemption or deferral of taxes on property of certain elderly individuals and individuals with disabilities
propertyTax.quote: governing body of any locality may, by ordinance, provide for the exemption from, deferral of | anyone at least 65 years of age | anyone found to be permanently and totally disabled

propertyTax.text: Virginia exempts the real property of a veteran rated 100 percent service-connected, permanent, and total disabled when it is the veteran's principal place of residence. A surviving spouse who does not remarry can also qualify, under the conditions in the statute.
propertyTax.source: Code of Virginia § 58.1-3219.5: Exemption from taxes on property for disabled veterans
propertyTax.quote: rated . . . to have a 100 percent service-connected, permanent, and total disability | his principal place of residence | shall also qualify for the exemption | the surviving spouse does not remarry

propertyTax.text: Washington offers a property tax reduction for senior citizens and people with disabilities. Applicants must be at least 61 or retired from regular gainful employment due to a disability, and have combined disposable income at or below the threshold for their county. The reduction depends on income, home value and local levy rates.
propertyTax.source: Washington Department of Revenue: property tax exemptions and deferrals
propertyTax.quote: At least 61 years of age or older. | Retired from regular gainful employment due to a disability. | have combined disposable income of Income Threshold 3 or less for your county. | The qualifying applicant receives a reduction in the amount of property taxes due. | The amount of the reduction is based on the applicant's income, the value of the residence, and the local levy rates.

propertyTax.text: A separate deferral program lets eligible homeowners age 60 or older (or retired due to a disability) postpone paying property taxes. Deferred amounts accrue 5% simple interest and are repaid when the home is sold, the owner dies, or the home stops being the primary residence.
propertyTax.source: Washington Department of Revenue: property tax exemptions and deferrals
propertyTax.quote: Taxpayers who are at least 60 years of age or older by December 31 of the year the application for deferral is filed. | allow payment of property taxes and special assessments for current and delinquent years. | The deferred amount accrues 5% simple interest until repayment is complete.

closing.text: Washington's state real estate excise tax rate depends on the sale price (rates effective January 1, 2023): 1.10% for $525,000 or less; 1.28% for $525,000.01 to $1,525,000; 2.75% for $1,525,000.01 to $3,025,000; and 3% for $3,025,000.01 or more. programs.source: Washington State Housing Finance Commission: Here to Home

programs.quote: 10-year fixed rate second mortgage with monthly payment | Minimum loan amount of $1,000 | Maximum loan amount is 6% of the purchase price when partnered with a WHEDA Conventional first mortgage loan

propertyTax.quote: must be a Wisconsin resident, own a dwelling and use it as your primary residence as of the January 1 certification date | The lottery and gaming credit is displayed on tax bills as a reduction of property taxes due.

programs.text: NIFA's First Home Program helps eligible first-time homebuyers purchase a home in Nebraska. The page says it may be a good fit if you are buying your first home, or if it has been three or more years since you owned and lived in a home as your primary residence.
programs.source: Nebraska Investment Finance Authority: First Home Program
programs.quote: The NIFA First Home Program helps eligible first-time homebuyers purchase a home in Nebraska. | This program may be a good fit if you are buying your first home, or if it has been three or more years since you owned and lived in a home as your primary residence.

closing.text: Nebraska's documentary stamp tax rate is $3.32 per each $1,000 of value or fraction thereof, effective July 18, 2026.
closing.source: Nebraska Department of Revenue: documentary stamp tax rate history
closing.quote: July 18, 2026 through current: $3.32 per each $1,000 of value or fraction thereof

closing.text: The tax is imposed on a grantor executing a deed for the privilege of recording the transfer.
closing.source: Nebraska Department of Revenue: documentary stamp tax
closing.quote: imposed on a grantor executing a deed for the privilege of recording the transfer.

closing.text: New Hampshire's real estate transfer tax is imposed on both the buyer and the seller at the rate of $0.75 per $100.
closing.source: New Hampshire Department of Revenue Administration: real estate transfer tax
closing.quote: The tax is imposed on both the buyer and the seller at the rate of $.75 per $100

programs.text: In an announcement effective August 1, 2024, New Hampshire Housing said downpayment assistance is available in fixed amounts of $5,000, $10,000, or $15,000, raising the previous cap from $10,000 to $15,000, for all qualifying homebuyers, not only first-time buyers. Confirm current terms with NH Housing.
programs.source: New Hampshire Housing: downpayment assistance announcement
programs.quote: fixed amounts of $5,000, $10,000, or $15,000 | raises the previous assistance cap from $10,000 to $15,000 | these new tiers are available to all qualifying homebuyers, not limited to only first-time buyers | effective August 1st (announcement dated August 1, 2024)

programs.text: RIHousing's 15kDPA program provides $15,000 in assistance for down payment and/or closing costs as a zero-percent (0%) interest rate loan to first-time homebuyers in Rhode Island. No monthly payments are due.
programs.quote: RIHousing's 15kDPA program provides $15,000 in assistance for down payment and/or closing costs | in the form of a zero-percent (0%) interest rate loan to first-time homebuyers in Rhode Island. | No monthly payments due

programs.text: Listed requirements include being a first-time homebuyer purchasing a 1-4 family home or condominium in Rhode Island, a minimum credit score of 660, a homebuyer education course, meeting RIHousing price and income limits, a RIHousing-funded first mortgage, and occupying the home as your primary residence.
programs.quote: Be a first-time homebuyer purchasing a 1-4 family home or condominium in Rhode Island | Have a minimum credit score of 660 | Complete a homebuyer education course | Must meet RIHousing Price and Income Limits

closing.text: Rhode Island's real estate conveyance tax is $3.75 for each $500 (or fraction thereof), up from $2.30, effective October 1, 2025.
closing.source: Rhode Island Division of Taxation: advisory 2025-13, conveyance tax increase
closing.quote: Rates increase from $2.30 to $3.75 per each $500 | The change is effective October 1, 2025.

closing.text: A second, higher tier applies when residential real property is conveyed for more than $800,000.
closing.source: Rhode Island Division of Taxation: advisory 2025-13, conveyance tax increase
closing.quote: a second tier (Tier 2) rate applies when Residential Real Property is conveyed for more than $800,000.

closing.text: The tax must be paid by the seller, grantor, assignor, transferor or person making the conveyance, unless there is an agreement with the purchaser to the contrary.
closing.source: Rhode Island Division of Taxation: real estate conveyance tax
closing.quote: The tax must be paid by the seller, grantor, assignor, transferor or person making the conveyance or vesting

programs.text: Montana's Bond Advantage down payment assistance can be used for down payment and closing costs, up to 5% of the sales price with a maximum of $15,000. It requires a Montana Board of Housing 30-year first mortgage, a minimum credit score of 620, homebuyer education, and at least $1,000 cash invested by the borrower.
programs.source: Montana Board of Housing: down payment assistance
programs.quote: Available for up to 5% of sales price, maximum $15,000 | Requires a Montana Board of Housing 30-year first mortgage, both loans have the same fixed rate | Minimum credit score of 620 for all borrowers | Homebuyer Education is required | Borrowers must provide a minimum of $1,000 cash investment in the purchase.

programs.text: The MBOH Plus 0% Deferred program offers a 0% second loan with no monthly payments, up to 5% of the sales price with a maximum of $15,000. The page lists a household income limit of $80,000 for 1-2 people and $90,000 for 3 or more, a minimum credit score of 620, and a maximum debt-to-income ratio of 45%.
programs.source: Montana Board of Housing: down payment assistance
programs.quote: 0% second loan, no monthly payments | Household income limit $80,000 for 1-2 people and $90,000 for 3+ people | Minimum credit score of 620, maximum Debt-to-Income (DTI) of 45% for all borrowers | Available for up to 5% of sales price, maximum $15,000

propertyTax.text: Montana's Homestead Reduced Rate gives qualifying owner-occupied homes a reduced tax rate compared to standard Class 4 residential property. Owners must occupy the home as their principal residence for at least seven months per year, and be current on property tax payments.
propertyTax.source: Montana Department of Revenue: Homestead Reduced Tax Rate FAQs
propertyTax.quote: carries a reduced tax rate compared to standard Class 4 residential property. | occupy their Montana home as their principal residence for at least seven months per year

propertyTax.text: Enrollment for the 2027 tax year closes on March 1, 2027. The Homestead Reduced Rate expires at the end of the calendar year.
propertyTax.source: Montana Department of Revenue: Homestead Reduced Tax Rate FAQs
propertyTax.quote: Homestead and long-term rental reduced tax rate enrollment is now open for the 2027 tax year. | closes on March 1, 2027.

programs.text: NDHFA's FirstHome program requires that you have not owned a home as your principal residence within the last three years and that you meet income and purchase price limits. The agency says all of its programs require a $500 out-of-pocket cash investment.
programs.source: North Dakota Housing Finance Agency: homeownership programs
programs.quote: You must not have owned a home as your principle residence within the last three years | You must meet income and purchase price limits. | All of our programs require a $500 out-of-pocket cash investment.

programs.text: NDHFA's DCA (down payment and closing cost assistance) equals three percent of the first mortgage loan amount. It cannot be used with other down payment assistance programs, requires a homebuyer education course, and is for one- to two-unit properties where one unit is occupied by the borrower.
programs.source: North Dakota Housing Finance Agency: homeownership programs
programs.quote: Amount of assistance equals three percent of the first mortgage loan amount | DCA cannot be used in conjunction with any other down payment assistance programs. | You must complete a homebuyer education course and receive a certificate of completion | Only one to two-unit properties (one unit must be occupied by borrower).

propertyTax.text: North Dakota's homestead property tax credit is for homeowners who are 65 or older or have a permanent and total disability, who live at and have an ownership interest in the property, and whose income, including a spouse and dependents, does not exceed $70,000.
propertyTax.source: North Dakota Office of State Tax Commissioner: homestead property tax credit
propertyTax.quote: 65 years of age or older, OR An individual with a permanent and total disability. | Live at and have an ownership interest in the property. | Not have income that exceeds $70,000, including the income of your spouse and any dependents.

propertyTax.text: With income of $0 to $40,000, taxable value is reduced by 100%, up to $9,000 of taxable value. With income of $40,001 to $70,000, it is reduced by 50%, up to $4,500 of taxable value.
propertyTax.source: North Dakota Office of State Tax Commissioner: homestead property tax credit
propertyTax.quote: Income $0–$40,000: taxable value reduced by 100%, up to $9,000 of taxable value | Income $40,001–$70,000: taxable value reduced by 50%, up to $4,500 of taxable value

propertyTax.text: Applications are due April 1 in the year in which the property is assessed and for which the credit is requested.
propertyTax.source: North Dakota Office of State Tax Commissioner: homestead property tax credit
propertyTax.quote: Applications are due April 1st in the year in which the property is assessed and for which the credit is requested.

agency.name: South Dakota Housing Development Authority (SD Housing)

programs.text: SD Housing's Fixed Rate Plus loan may provide 3% or 5% in downpayment and closing costs assistance, as a second mortgage at 0% interest rate, due-on-sale or satisfaction, with no payments and no additional fees. Ask your lender to see if you qualify.
programs.quote: If you qualify, you may receive 3% or 5% in downpayment and closing costs assistance to help with financing your mortgage. | will include a second mortgage at 0% interest rate, due-on-sale or satisfaction, no payments and no additional fees.

propertyTax.text: South Dakota's assessment freeze for the elderly and disabled requires you to be 65 or older or disabled, and to have owned an owner-occupied single-family dwelling and been a South Dakota resident for five years (unless you received the freeze the previous year). Income and property value limits apply, and applications go to the county treasurer on or before April 1.
propertyTax.source: South Dakota Department of Revenue: property tax relief programs
propertyTax.quote: You must be 65 years of age or older OR disabled | You must have been an owner of an owner-occupied single-family dwelling and a resident of South Dakota for five years, unless you received the assessment freeze in the previous year. | Income and property value limits apply. | on or before April 1st

programs.text: VHFA's ASSIST down payment assistance is up to a $10,000 loan for down payment and closing assistance, as a 0% deferred loan with no monthly payments. It is available exclusively with VHFA MOVE, and borrowers and non-borrowing spouses must have never owned a home and have less than $20,000 combined liquid assets.
programs.source: Vermont Housing Finance Agency: loan programs
programs.quote: Up to $10,000 loan for down payment and closing assistance | 0% deferred loan with no monthly payments | Borrowers and non-borrowing spouses must have NEVER owned a home and have less than $20,000 combined liquid assets | Available exclusively with VHFA MOVE.

programs.text: The First Generation Homebuyer Grant is a $15,000 grant for down payment and closing costs. It is available exclusively with VHFA MOVE, MOVE MCC, or ADVANTAGE.
programs.source: Vermont Housing Finance Agency: loan programs
programs.quote: $15,000 grant for down payment and closing costs | Available exclusively with VHFA MOVE, MOVE MCC, or ADVANTAGE.

programs.text: A Mortgage Credit Certificate (MCC) is a federal tax credit of up to 50% of mortgage interest paid annually, capped at $2,000 per year. Other credit and property eligibility requirements apply.
programs.source: Vermont Housing Finance Agency: loan programs
programs.quote: Federal tax credit up to 50% of mortgage interest paid annually, capped at $2,000 per year

closing.text: Vermont's property transfer tax general rate is 1.25%. A separate 0.22% Clean Water Surcharge also applies.
closing.source: Vermont Department of Taxes: property transfer tax
closing.quote: General Tax Rate: 1.25%. | 0.22% Clean Water Surcharge

closing.text: For a principal residence, the first $200,000 of value paid is subject to the 0.5% Principal Residence Tax Rate.
closing.source: Vermont Department of Taxes: property transfer tax
closing.quote: Principal Residence Tax Rate: 0.5%. | The first $200,000 of value paid is subject to 0.5% Principal Residence Tax Rate.

programs.text: A WVHDF Homeownership Program Loan is a 30-year, fixed rate mortgage loan, and up to 100% of the purchase price of the home can be financed.
programs.source: West Virginia Housing Development Fund: Homeownership Program
programs.quote: A Homeownership Program Loan is a 30-year, fixed rate mortgage loan. | Up to 100% of the purchase price of the home can be financed.

programs.text: Borrower gross income must not exceed a county income limit, and the house must not exceed a house price limit. In certain counties the borrower cannot have owned a home within the prior three years.
programs.source: West Virginia Housing Development Fund: Homeownership Program
programs.quote: Borrower(s) gross income must not exceed a county income limit; | The house to be purchased must not exceed a house price limit; | cannot have owned a home within the prior three years

propertyTax.text: The first $20,000 of assessed value of owner-occupied residential property owned by a person age 65 or older, or by a person who is permanently and totally disabled, is exempt.
propertyTax.source: West Virginia State Tax Department: property tax exemptions
propertyTax.quote: The first $20,000 of assessed value of owner-occupied residential property | owned by a person age 65 or older or by a person who is permanently and totally disabled is exempt.

programs.text: WCDA's down payment assistance products list a $15,000 maximum loan amount, a 620 minimum credit score, and a $1,500 minimum borrower contribution (which may be a gift).
programs.quote: $15,000 maximum loan amount | 620 minimum credit score | $1,500 minimum borrower contribution required (may be a gift)

programs.text: WCDA's Advantage loan is a 30-year fixed rate mortgage with no first-time homebuyer requirement. It lists a minimum credit score of 620 and requires you to occupy the property as your principal residence for at least one year.
programs.quote: 30-year fixed rate mortgage | No first-time homebuyer requirement | Minimum credit score of 620 | Must occupy property as principal residence for at least one year

programs.text: WCDA's First-Time Home Buyer loan requires no ownership interest in a primary residence in the last 3 years.
programs.quote: Must meet first-time homebuyer (FTHB) requirement of no ownership interest in a primary residence in the last 3 years

propertyTax.text: Wyoming assesses residential property at 9.5% of market value.
propertyTax.source: Wyoming Department of Revenue, Property Tax Division: residential
propertyTax.quote: Residential property is assessed at 9.5% of market value.
